hypothesis: If Darwin is right that the migratory instinct varies within species in extent and may be lost, then partial migration (some individuals or populations of a species migrate while others of the same species stay resident) is a common condition among birds rather than a rare anomaly, and species classified as partial migrants show measurably more winter presence inside their breeding latitudes than obligate migrants do.
pass_criterion: Primary (AVONET, Tobias et al. 2022, BirdLife taxonomy sheet): P = share of bird species with a coded Migration score that are coded 2 (partially migratory) among all species, and Q = share coded 2 among non-sedentary species (score 2 or 3). Secondary (GBIF occurrence counts, Northern Hemisphere, years 2000 onward, non-fossil non-captive records, 5-degree latitude bands 0-80 N): for 12 pre-registered species, W = fraction of December-February records that fall in the latitude bands holding the central 80 % of June-July records (winter residency index). Partial-migrant set: Erithacus rubecula, Turdus merula, Sylvia atricapilla, Fringilla coelebs, Sturnus vulgaris, Turdus migratorius. Obligate-migrant set: Hirundo rustica, Apus apus, Phylloscopus trochilus, Setophaga striata, Tyrannus tyrannus, Cuculus canorus. Supports if P >= 0.20 and W is higher in the partial-migrant set than in the obligate set by a one-sided Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05 with median W of the partial set >= 0.25.
fail_criterion: Refutes if P < 0.05 (within-species variation in migratory extent is a rare anomaly) or if the obligate set has median W >= the partial set (the trait classification does not correspond to any measurable difference in winter residency). Otherwise mixed. The nest-construction clause is not tested (no public, geographically coded nest-architecture dataset at the within-species level was identified) and is recorded as untested in caveats.
interpretation: Darwin's examples of instinct variation are migration (extent, direction, total loss) and nest form; this test addresses the migration example only. 'Varies within species in a state of nature' is operationalised as partial migration: a species whose populations or individuals differ in whether or how far they migrate. AVONET's Migration score (1 sedentary, 2 partially migratory, 3 migratory) is an expert synthesis from handbooks; it is used for the global prevalence P. The GBIF index W checks that this classification corresponds to an observable pattern: a species whose individuals all migrate should have few winter records at breeding latitudes, whereas a partial migrant retains many. Recent records (2000 onward) are used because eBird dominates GBIF bird data and gives dense year-round coverage; the Northern Hemisphere restriction avoids mixing austral seasons. Latitude bands are global in longitude, so for species occurring on more than one continent (Sturnus vulgaris, introduced in North America) the index pools populations. Thresholds: 20 % of all bird species being partial migrants is taken as 'common'; 5 % as 'rare'. Direction of migration and the evolutionary loss of migration are not measured separately, since occurrence data cannot attribute a wintering bird to its breeding population.
